headline: Southborough approved comprehensive permit conditions for 32 townhouse units at 250 Turnpike Road and authorized $12.5 million in regional dispatch borrowing.
synopsis: In May 2026, town boards advanced major housing, facility, and infrastructure projects across Southborough. The Zoning Board of Appeals approved comprehensive permit conditions for a 32-unit Chapter 40B townhouse development at 250 Turnpike Road, while the Select Board authorized up to $12.5 million in bridge borrowing for the MetroWest regional emergency dispatch center. School leaders moved forward on building plans, awarding the Neary School feasibility study design contract to Tappe Architects and addressing an urgent, multi-million-dollar roof replacement needed at Neary. The Planning Board enacted new landscape regulations requiring 100 percent native vegetation for site plan projects and recommended revoking temporary occupancy for 40-42 Central Street. Meanwhile, the School Committee endorsed a 3.99 percent operating budget increase for FY27 alongside planned technology and security capital upgrades.

top_items.title: Comprehensive permit approved for 250 Turnpike Road 40B
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to approve comprehensive permit conditions and waivers for a 32-unit rental townhouse project.
top_items.body: Town special counsel presented the draft comprehensive permit decision, findings of fact, and conditions for the development at 250 Turnpike Road and 9 Parkerville Road. The 32 rental townhouses include eight affordable units restricted to households earning up to 80 percent of area median income, with conditions governing stormwater management, traffic, school bus accommodation, and wetland buffer protection.

top_items.title: Select Board approves $12.5 million emergency dispatch borrowing
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 4-1 to authorize up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
top_items.body: The borrowing acts as a bridge loan to allow regional dispatch construction contracts to continue without disruption between state 911 development grant disbursements. One member opposed Southborough taking on borrowing risk for the regional district, while others noted member communities Grafton and Westborough had already approved it.

top_items.title: Neary School feasibility study design contract awarded
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to award the Neary Elementary School feasibility study design contract to Tappe Architects.
top_items.body: The Elementary School Building Committee evaluated five designer proposals and interviewed three finalists before recommending Tappe Architects based on their school design experience and community engagement approach. The Select Board approved the recommendation and authorized the committee to negotiate contract terms.

top_items.title: Failing Neary School roof evaluated for full replacement
top_items.why: Structural consultants reported Neary Elementary School's 30-year-old roof is in active failure, recommending a replacement estimated at $4.5 million to $6.5 million.
top_items.body: SOCOTEC engineers identified approximately 8,000 linear feet of failed seams, extensive water intrusion, and 22,000 square feet of detached insulation, advising against patch repairs. The School Committee reviewed short-term sandbag stabilization and examined capital warrant strategies, including state accessibility thresholds that could add over $2 million in building-wide ADA upgrades if triggered.

top_items.title: Planning Board adopts mandatory Native Landscape Regulations
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to adopt new regulations mandating native plants and prohibiting neonicotinoids for site plan review projects.
top_items.body: Drafted in collaboration with the Open Space Preservation Commission, the rules require 100 percent of new vegetation in site plan reviews to consist of native species. The regulations also prohibit neonicotinoid pesticides and place restrictions on dyed mulches and invasive plant species.

top_items.title: School Committee endorses 3.99% FY27 budget increase
top_items.why: The Southborough School Committee voted 4-0 to support a revised recommended FY27 operating budget carrying a 3.99 percent increase.
top_items.body: Budget revisions included lowering the applied circuit breaker reserve drawdown from $500,000 to $300,000, restoring facilities accounts, and adding a third-grade section. These costs were offset by staff retirement savings and reduced out-of-district tuition.

top_items.title: Planning Board recommends revoking 40-42 Central Street occupancy
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted 4-1 to recommend that the Building Commissioner revoke the temporary certificate of occupancy for 40-42 Central Street.
top_items.body: Board members cited ongoing non-compliance by the Southborough Historical Society regarding site plan conditions under its temporary occupancy permit. Deficiencies included unresolved accessible parking layouts, unaddressed parking lot lighting, outstanding peer review fees, and failure to submit formal site plan modifications.
